title: Deduction Management: The Five Root-Cause Categories Explained
summary: Every retailer deduction traces back to one of five root causes. This glossary breaks down each category, with real examples and prevention tips.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


The five root-cause categories behind nearly every retailer deduction


-


Why the same root cause shows up under a different code at every retailer


-


How to prevent the errors that lead to deductions


---


Every retailer names deductions differently.[Walmart](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/walmart-deduction-codes) , for instance, uses numeric deduction codes, whereas[Amazon](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/categories/amazon-deductions) splits revenue loss into shortage claims and chargebacks and[Home Depot](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/home-depot-deduction-types-remittance-list-and-contact-information) tags each deduction with its own invoice-field code. If you’re an analyst working across several retailers, you’ll need to learn several sets of vocabularies to figure out what happened to a single payment.


Making matters more complicated, the differences in naming are just the surface level. Underneath, almost every deduction comes from one of five root-cause categories. Those categories are:


-


Operational errors


-


Administrative mismatches


-


[Advance ship notice](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-document/edi-856-advance-shipping-notice/) (ASN) or[electronic data interchange](https://www.spscommerce.com/what-is-edi/) (EDI) problems


-


Carrier or delivery failures


-


Compliance gaps


Once a new code fits into the right category, tracking deductions across retailers ceases to be a new investigation, and instead turns into pattern recognition.


## What Are the Five Root-Cause Categories Behind Retailer Deductions?


### 1. Operational Errors


Operational errors happen at the warehouse, before a shipment leaves the dock. These errors include shipment shortages, mispacks, wrong unit counts, and carton configuration mistakes.


**Example:**[Target's Deduction Code A030](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/target-deduction-codes-at-a-high-level) is a manual deduction for a carton shortage: the gap between what was invoiced and what was received.


**What you need to prevent it:** A[bill of lading](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/bill-lading-bol-supplypike) (BOL) and[proof of delivery](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-proof-of-delivery) (POD) that match the shipped quantity give a supplier the paper trail to catch and dispute an operational error before it happens again.


### 2. Administrative Errors


Administrative errors are in the paperwork. They include invoice discrepancies, pricing mismatches between the[invoice](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-document/edi-810-electronic-invoice/) and the[purchase order](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-document/edi-850-purchase-order/) (PO), and wrong item information.


**Example:**[Target's Deduction Code A036](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/target-deduction-codes-at-a-high-level) covers a cost gap between the invoice and the PO. Target requires written buyer approval of the correct cost before a supplier can dispute it.


**What you need to prevent it:** A PO-to-invoice match, run before the invoice goes out, catches a pricing or cost mismatch while it’s still cheap to fix.


### 3. ASN and EDI Errors


This category covers ASNs that are late, missing, or wrong, plus EDI documents missing a required data field. Retailers often require the ASN to transmit within a narrow window before[the shipment reaches the distribution center](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-read-a-routing-guide-without-missing-the-rules-that-cost-you) . A missing or malformed Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC) segment can trigger a chargeback even when the physical shipment is correct.


**Example:**[Amazon's On-Time Non-Compliance](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-prevent-amazon-asn-chargebacks) (OTNC) chargeback triggers when a supplier's ASN transmits after Amazon's required window, even if the shipment itself arrives on time. Amazon generally expects the ASN within 30 minutes of shipment departure, or at least six hours before the scheduled delivery appointment.


**What you need to prevent it:** Checking ASN timing and data accuracy against the retailer's transmission window, before the carrier picks up the shipment, stops this before it reaches the deduction stage.


### 4. Carrier and Delivery Failures


Carrier and delivery failures cover late deliveries, missed appointment or reschedule windows, incorrect carriers, and paperwork errors that affect proof of delivery.


**Example:** Home Depot tags several of these failures with their own invoice-field codes, including a[Fleet Deduction code and a separate Prepaid Freight code](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/home-depot-deduction-types-remittance-list-and-contact-information) . Each one routes to its own department.


**What you need to prevent it:** Reviewing the retailer's routing guide and double-checking carrier compliance before shipping catches most of this before delivery even happens.


### 5. Compliance Gaps


Compliance gaps cover labeling errors, pallet configuration violations, and missed packaging specs.


**Example:** At Amazon, a shipping label that does not match its ASN causes a scan failure. Amazon[calls this a No Carton Content Label, or No CCL](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/labeling-for-new-suppliers-gs1-128-sscc-and-where-labels-have-to-go) , and charges a fee to cover the manual labor of processing the shipment by hand.


**What you need to prevent it:** Checking a shipment's[GS1-128 labels](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-document/ucc-128-label/) against both the retailer's spec and the ASN itself, before the carton leaves the dock, stops one labeling mistake from repeating across an entire shipment.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is a deduction the same thing as a chargeback?


Not always. The terms vary by retailer. Some retailers use "deduction" for any withheld payment. Others, including Amazon, use "chargeback" for compliance issues and "shortage claim" for quantity disputes. The five root-cause categories apply across all of these terms, because they describe the failure itself rather than the retailer's label for it.


### Which root-cause category is the most common?


It depends on the retailer, the product category, and the supplier's own supply chain maturity. No single category is universally the largest. Suppliers who log the root cause on every dispute can see which category drives the most volume in their own history.


### Can one deduction have more than one root cause?


Yes. A late ASN can trigger a compliance chargeback at one retailer and an operational shortage claim at another if the delayed paperwork also caused a receiving mismatch. When a deduction straddles two categories, log the more specific cause, specifically the one closest to where the process actually broke.


### Does this framework apply outside major retailers like Walmart, Amazon, and Target?


Yes. The five categories describe the operational and paperwork failures that generate deductions industry-wide. The retailer-specific codes in this glossary are examples and are not the limit of where the framework applies.
